calls.video_title: Massive News for Anthropic Stock Investors as IPO is Hugely Successful  | ANT Stock Analysis
calls.price_at_call: $83 IPO price (waiting for shares to settle; no entry level stated)
calls.thesis: CONDITIONAL_BUY, first tracked for Parkevtate. 'Very interested in owning shares' of 'one of the best AI companies in the market right now' and the only pure-play large-language-model/agentic-AI platform, but 'not interested in the early days' — waiting for the shares to settle down and for more information before deciding to buy. Expects the IPO pattern seen with SpaceX: an initial jump, then a pullback and settle. The ~$100bn raise (public + private) takes cash above $200bn, enough to reach a self-sustaining, cash-flow-neutral footing and fund next-gen models and inference.
calls.base_case: Anthropic keeps growing anywhere near current rates, reaches cash-flow neutral, and keeps buying compute — good news for the whole AI ecosystem (NVDA, AMD, Micron, Intel, Broadcom, TSMC, SK Hynix).
calls.bull_case: Growth stays extraordinary, computing efficiency keeps improving, and the platform becomes an enterprise/consumer software platform — 'significant growth ahead'.
calls.bear_case: Shares jump then settle well below the open (as SpaceX did after $200+), or Anthropic comes back to market for more capital despite the raise.

calls.thesis: AVOID first tracked. Not a buyer today or in the near future at a ~$1.5-1.6T valuation despite $17B last-quarter revenue and 10x YoY growth; prefers the four names below instead.
calls.base_case: FY26 revenue $56B, FY27 $144.7B, FY28 $270.3B expected; cash from operations just turned positive.
calls.bull_case: Growth re-accelerates toward 40%+ QoQ and margins hold as token prices fall.
calls.bear_case: Cash burn rises as gigawatts come online; token-price deflation squeezes margins.

calls.thesis: CONDITIONAL_BUY, first tracked for Roussin. Likes the business (revenue $33.2bn in 9M 2026, +1,200% YoY; $81bn annualised run rate; operating loss narrowing to $1.3bn) but will NOT chase the IPO: expects a first-day pop then profit-taking and will likely play options to the downside (as he did with SpaceX). Would consider buying only if the valuation becomes attractive down the road. ~$1.5tn valuation is ~18.5x annualised sales / 16.9x EV/sales - all future growth already priced in.
calls.base_case: IPO pops on strong demand, then gives back gains in the first 12 months (major IPOs average ~49% first-day pop, ~55% max drawdown in year one).
calls.bull_case: Revenue growth stays extraordinary, margins expand and FCF follows, justifying a premium valuation.
calls.bear_case: Growth slows, competition (OpenAI, Gemini) pressures Claude, or model costs stay high - no room for disappointment at this price.
